title: Do Not Go Past the Mark You Aimed For; In Victory, Learn When to Stop
coreMove: Stop after the achieved mark before victory turns appetite into reversal
sourcePressure: Chapter 47 centers on the danger of overreaching after success. The law argues that victory often creates its own risk when a person keeps pushing past the point that already secured the goal. Its practical claim is that restraint after success can preserve gains, while excess, triumph, or one move too many can convert victory into reversal. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
